newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends up on crushers, funds, exporters.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends up on crushers, funds, exporters.

text.p: WCE canola ended up on crusher, fund and exporter demand, traders said.
"UGG's bought for exporters, crushers are buying August and September and funds bought mostly May," a trader said. "Crushers and funds bought between 1,500 to 2,000 contracts."

March canola futures crush margin rose to a new crop year high of -18.19 Thursday from -21.01 Wednesday. March-May spread at $1, Sep-Nov $7, Mar-Nov $40.50. Volume was 6,350 lots, or 127,000 tonnes, with 820 hedges.
Japan bought 4,000-5,000 tonnes overnight, sources said.
March canola rose $3.90 to $412.50. Oats did not trade.
November flax rose $1 to $350.50 on commercial demand.
March feed wheat rose $1.10 to $166.60 on commercials but the bulk of the volume came from spreads with the Mar-July at $5, Mar-May $3, July-Dec $6. Volume was 1,575 lots.
March western barley rose $0.90 to $137.50 on commercial and Pool demand, May rose $0.80 to $137.70 with legging of the July, Oct and Dec contracts, traders said. Volume was 1,150 lots.
May feed peas rose US$1 to US$200.50 on commercials.
(Values in Canadian dollars/tonne except oats and peas.)
